nodes.title: Policy Revival, Non-Forfeiture Benefits, and Reduced Paid-Up Provisions
key_items: D.3. 2. All the benefits under the Policy shall be restored on the Revival of Lapsed/Reduced Paid-up Policy.
nodes.summary: The page covers revival provisions for lapsed or reduced paid-up policies, including the revival interest rate calculation based on the 10-year benchmark G-Sec yield plus 2%, reset half-yearly, and the current 9.5% compounding rate. It details revival campaigns with possible reduced interest rates and rebates, and the payment of overdue annuities upon revival. It states that all benefits are restored upon revival, and the Company may revive on original or modified terms, reject revival, or require medical examination. Revival takes effect upon written communication. If not revived within five years and no Guaranteed Surrender Value, the policy terminates. Non-Forfeiture Benefits are not applicable for Single Premium policies. For Limited Premium Policies, forfeiture occurs if at least the first full year's premium is not paid; otherwise, the policyholder is eligible for Reduced Paid-up Value and Surrender Value. Cancellation/Surrender is not allowed for annuity policies from NPS exit proceeds. Reduced Paid-up Value conditions and revised annuity rate are also covered.

nodes.title: Surrender Benefit and Surrender Value Provisions
nodes.summary: The page outlines the surrender benefit and surrender value provisions for HDFC Life Smart Pension Plus. It states that the policy cannot be surrendered after the annuitant's death and only during the policy term, with termination upon payment of surrender value. Cancellation/surrender is not allowed for annuity policies from NPS exit proceeds except in specific exceptional cases per PFRDA regulations, with remittance to Trustee Bank. The surrender value is the higher of Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV). GSV applies immediately for Single Pay and after two years for Limited Pay, only for policies with deferment option during deferment period, calculated as GSV Factor times total premiums paid, with factors increasing with policy duration.

nodes.title: D.9. Liquidity Option:
nodes.summary: HDFC Life Smart Pension Plus (UIN - 101N173V13) is a non-linked, non-participating individual annuity savings plan. On the annuitant's death, annuity payments stop, and premiums are refunded to purchase a new annuity for living dependent parents, prioritizing the mother, then father, under Plan Option B with 100% Return of Total Premiums Paid on a Single Life basis at prevailing rates. This continues until all specified family members are covered; thereafter, premiums go to surviving children, else legal heirs, or nominee if none exist. Premiums exclude loadings, taxes, statutory levies, and rider premiums. For NPS subscribers, free-look returns funds to the Central Recordkeeping Agency for re-allocation upon selecting an Annuity Service Provider. The Liquidity Option (D.9) allows a lumpsum for reduced annuity and benefits, only under Plan Option B with 100% Return of Total Premiums Paid, exercisable after 5 years from first payout, up to 3 times, with total lumpsum not exceeding 60% of premiums paid, subject to IRDAI minimum limits (2024). Post-exercise, annuity rate, death benefit, and other benefits are revised from withdrawal date, and surrender benefit is based on revised rates. The Advanced Annuity Option (D.10) permits withdrawing present value of annuities for the next 1 to 5 years as a lump sum, with policyholder choosing the period and percentage (x%) to advance. It is available only for Joint Life under ‘Life Annuity with Return of % of Total Premiums Paid’ variant on first death amongst annuitants, exercisable within 6 months of that death. If exercised, lump sum is paid immediately, and annuity for the advance period continues for the balance ((1-x%) of annuity payable).

nodes.title: D.10. Advanced Annuity Option:
nodes.summary: The text describes HDFC Life Smart Pension Plus, a non-linked non-participating individual annuity savings plan. It covers death benefit provisions where premiums are refunded to purchase a new annuity for dependent parents in a specified order, with continuation until all family members are covered, then return to children, legal heirs, or nominee. It details the Liquidity Option allowing lumpsum withdrawals under Plan Option B with conditions on timing, frequency, amount, and impact on benefits.
